sections.report-regulatory:
D10 Regulatory currency. Statutory references reflect the law and guidance as at 2026-10-08 for the pathway and lodgement date shown. Under the Planning Act 2026, consents lodged before 30 October 2026 are processed under the RMA as it stood immediately before 30 September 2026, and those lodged later are processed under the amended RMA as at lodgement. The specified transition date to the new planning system has not been set. This report is not legal or planning advice. Confirm the applicable provisions at lodgement.
D11 Authorities. Since 7 May 2026 Auckland Council is the road controlling authority for Auckland roads (Local Government (Auckland Council) Act 2009 s47), with local boards exercising specified powers on local and collector roads and Auckland Transport continuing as the transport CCO for public transport. AUP provisions that still refer to Auckland Transport are quoted as written. Confirm the reviewing and approving body for this application.

sections.report-modelling:
Spare Construct assigns peak-hour vehicle demand (gravity distribution with gateway through-traffic) to the network by conjugate Frank-Wolfe user equilibrium, with BPR link times (α 0.15, β 4) and HCM 6 / Akçelik junction delay. Background growth: linear, 1.5% of 2026 volume per year. Convergence target: relative gap 0.010% with the TAG M3.1 stability rule, at most 200 iterations. Full inputs are in Appendix A.

Every stored run converged to its target (Appendix B).

MSM consistency not checked: AT ITA v2 s4.2.1.1 expects consistency with MSM forecasts where appropriate.

D7 Regional consistency. The AT ITA Guidelines 2025 v2 expect detailed modelling to be consistent with regional MSM forecasts where appropriate. Where this report states that MSM consistency was not checked, the forecasts should be reconciled with MSM or Auckland Forecasting Centre outputs before lodgement for any proposal with network-wide effects.
sections.report-walk: Author to complete. Assess public transport, walking and cycling levels of service with the proposal (AT ITA s4.2.1).
sections.report-extent: The extent test needs a without and a with scenario for the same year, both run for the same period. No same-year without scenario was found for Do-minimum 2036 (2036). Set them in the Report tab and run both.
sections.report-junctions: The junction flow-scale test (+10% on every movement) follows this section, then turning movement diagrams for the key junctions; per-turn movement summaries are in Appendix C. The sensitivity pack (section 4.6) re-runs the whole network with trip rates and total demand ±10% and background growth ±50%.
sections.junctions-performance:
Junction flow-scale test (+10%)

No junction crosses its practical degree of saturation when flows rise by 10%.

Flow-scale test: TTOC-06 Traffic Signals Modelling Guidelines. Junctions are re-evaluated at flows × 1.10 with each run's signal timings; routes are not re-assigned. HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, indicative; not SIDRA output.

With the proposal, all 2 assessed junctions operate within practical DoS in the 2036 AM and PM peaks; the worst is Row 1 1 / Row 1 2 / Col 2 0 (DoS 0.27, LoS A, AM peak). Junction results are indicative (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based), not SIDRA output.

D1 Screening status. Spare Construct is a browser-based sketch and screening tool. It is not an approved regional transport model and it is not the Auckland Forecasting Centre Macro Strategic Model (MSM). Its results are indicative and are intended to scope, test and support a transport assessment. It is equivalent to an Indicative Efficiency Rating, not a funding-approval BCR. It is not MBCM-compliant unless the full procedures are applied to a model calibrated and validated to the NZTA Transport Model Development Guidelines and independently reviewed. Those criteria are not a pass/fail checklist, and meeting them does not by itself make a model fit for purpose. 4.2 Model description and calibration summaryauto

Spare Construct assigns peak-hour vehicle demand (gravity distribution with gateway through-traffic) to the network by conjugate Frank-Wolfe user equilibrium, with BPR link times (α 0.15, β 4) and HCM 6 / Akçelik junction delay. Background growth: linear, 1.5% of 2026 volume per year. Convergence target: relative gap 0.010% with the TAG M3.1 stability rule, at most 200 iterations. Full inputs are in Appendix A.

﻿"# Spare Construct ITA data pack, by-scenario/truth-test-grid-base-case-am-2026-links.csv: Base case, AM peak hour, 2026 (the columns of links.csv). Spare Construct is a browser-based sketch and screening tool. It is not an approved regional transport model and it is not the Auckland Forecasting Centre Macro Strategic Model (MSM). Its results are indicative and are intended to scope, test and support a transport assessment. They must be reviewed, and where necessary confirmed with approved tools, by a suitably qualified transport planner or traffic engineer before they are relied on in any resource consent, plan change, notice of requirement, Fast-track application or funding decision."

pack.name: load_corridor_volumes.py
read_datapack.py
pack.data:
# Spare Construct is a browser-based sketch and screening tool. It is not an approved regional transport model and it is not the Auckland Forecasting Centre Macro Strategic Model (MSM). Its results are indicative and are intended to scope, test and support a transport assessment. They must be reviewed, and where necessary confirmed with approved tools, by a suitably qualified transport planner or traffic engineer before they are relied on in any resource consent, plan change, notice of requirement, Fast-track application or funding decision.
# Load Spare Construct ITA data pack CSVs in Python (standard library only).
# Every CSV is UTF-8 with a BOM, and its first row is Disclaimer D1: skip it.
# pandas: pd.read_csv(path, encoding='utf-8-sig', skiprows=1)
import csv, sys

def load(path):
    with open(path, encoding='utf-8-sig', newline='') as f:
        rows = list(csv.reader(f))
    if rows and rows[0] and rows[0][0].startswith('#'):
        rows = rows[1:]
    head, body = rows[0], rows[1:]
    return [dict(zip(head, r)) for r in body]

if __name__ == '__main__':
    path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'links.csv'
    data = load(path)
    print(f'{len(data)} rows from {path}')
    for row in data[:10]:
        print(row)
